procedures.title: Clean the dishwasher filter
procedures.safety_note: Turn the dishwasher off first, and watch for broken glass or sharp debris in the sump.
steps: Turn the dishwasher off and open the door.
Slide out the bottom rack so you can reach the floor of the tub.
Find the round filter in the floor of the tub and twist it counter-clockwise, then lift it out.
Rinse the filter under warm running water and brush away any food debris.
Wipe out the opening underneath, checking for glass, seeds or bits of label.
Put the filter back and twist it clockwise until it seats firmly. A loose filter is the most common mistake.
Slide the rack back in and run a short rinse cycle to check that the water drains.

procedures.title: Replace the furnace air filter
tools_needed: a new 20 by 25 by 1 inch MERV 11 filter
procedures.safety_note: Switch the furnace off at its service switch or breaker before opening any panel.
steps: Turn the furnace off at the service switch on its side, or at the breaker.
Open the blower door panel, usually the lower front panel.
Before pulling the old filter out, look at the arrow printed on its frame and note which way it points.
Slide the old filter out.
Slide the new filter in with its arrow pointing the same way, toward the blower.
Close the panel and turn the furnace back on.

procedures.title: Replace the refrigerator water filter
procedures.safety_note: Expect a small amount of water to spill when the old filter comes out.
steps: Find the filter housing, usually inside the fridge at the top right or behind the bottom grille.
Put a towel underneath, then turn the old filter a quarter turn counter-clockwise and pull it straight out.
Take the cap off the new filter and push it in, then turn it clockwise until it stops.
Run about two gallons of water through the dispenser into a jug to clear air and carbon dust.
Hold the filter reset button for three seconds to clear the indicator light.

procedures.title: Run a washer cleaning cycle
tools_needed: a washer cleaning tablet or two cups of white vinegar
procedures.safety_note: Run this cycle empty. Never mix vinegar with bleach.
steps: Take everything out of the drum and check that it is empty.
Wipe the rubber door seal, folding it back to reach the underside where residue collects.
Put a cleaning tablet in the empty drum, or two cups of white vinegar in the detergent drawer.
Run the Tub Clean or Clean Washer cycle, or the hottest normal cycle if there is no clean setting.
When it finishes, wipe the drum dry and leave the door open so it can air out.

symptoms.symptom: will not drain, standing water in the bottom

causes.cause: The filter is clogged with food debris.
The drain hose is kinked or blocked.
A new garbage disposal still has its knockout plug in place.
The air filter is dirty and restricting airflow.
Supply vents are closed or blocked by furniture.
The blower motor or capacitor is failing.

symptoms.symptom: dispenser water tastes bad or runs slowly

causes.cause: The water filter is past its service life.
Air is trapped in the water line after a recent filter change.
The supply line is partly kinked behind the fridge.

symptoms.symptom: musty or mildew smell from the drum

causes.cause: Residue has built up in the drum and door seal.
The door is kept closed between washes, trapping moisture.
The drain pump filter is holding stagnant water.
